newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia frees ex-officer, treason charge stands. [corrected 13:04 gmt 15/12]
newsitem.headline: Russia frees ex-officer, treason charge stands. [corrected 13:04 gmt 15/12]

text.p: A retired Russian navy captain imprisoned for almost a year on suspicion of revealing state secrets to a Norwegian environmental group has been freed but the charges against him still stand, his lawyer said on Sunday.
Yuri Schmidt (corrects spelling of name) said Alexander Nikitin was still charged with treason but his release from prison marked the first step towards victory in the case.
"The charge has not been lifted, but it will be and this is the first step, a very important step," Schmidt said by telephone from St Petersburg.
He did not say why the authorities had decided to release Nikitin, dubbed Russia's first post-communist political prisoner by international human rights groups.

Russian officials were not immediately available for comment, but Interfax news agency said Nikitin's release was procedural, linked to the end of a preliminary investigation and the transfer of the case to the city prosecutor's office.

In Oslo, a spokeswoman for Norway's Bellona environmental organisation told Reuters that Nikitin was freed released at 1735 p.m. Moscow time (1435 GMT) from prison in St. Petersburg on orders from Russia's chief prosecutor.

"We have talked to Nikitin and he said he will first fight to finish the court case and win full freedom. He looks forward to contuinuing the work to contain radioactive pollution on the Kola peninsula," said the spokeswoman, Siri Engerseth.
Nikitin wrote about the hazards posed by the nuclear submarines of Russia's Northern Fleet in a report published earlier this year by Bellona.
He was arrested in February but formal charges were not brought until October, a year after the Federal Security Service (FSB) raided Bellona's offices in the Arctic port of Murmansk.

It confiscated computers, data discs and other material and said later some of them contained state secrets, an allegation denied by Bellona, which is carrying out research into the risks of the ageing fleet on Norway's doorstep.
The FSB said in October Nikitin had been charged on three counts -- treason, revealing state secrets and forgery.
FSB sources said he continued to use his military identification card to gain access to top secret documents on Bellona's behalf after he was retired from active service.
